- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:88-89 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `FOCUS_JOB_RE` requires the job name to end immediately after `codex-agent`, so it misses review jobs with a parenthesized suffix and the collector skips them without collecting logs.
  WHY: Suffixed review jobs can reproduce the runs=0 symptom the PR is intended to fix.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:270 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The intake jq filter requires the job name to end immediately after `codex-agent`, so it misses review jobs with a parenthesized suffix and reads no job logs.
  WHY: Autofix reports for suffixed review jobs can produce no logs for the diagnosis prompt, reproducing the runs=0 failure.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:696-709 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `Collector.lineage()` does not deduplicate issues across pagination pages before constructing GraphQL aliases, so duplicate issue numbers can make GitHub reject the query and skip all related closing-PR lookups.
  WHY: The reviewers disagreed on severity; the highest rating is major because a duplicate alias can omit all lineage PR data for the collection.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:825-850 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `Collector.lineage()` does not deduplicate issues across pagination pages before constructing GraphQL aliases, so duplicate issue numbers can make GitHub reject the query and skip all related closing-PR lookups.
  WHY: Duplicate aliases cause the GraphQL query to fail, losing closing-PR references for the entire lineage.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:689-693 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The fallback `none (review job)` labels any empty `failing_step` as a review job, including non-review jobs that failed without a step-level failure.
  WHY: This can misdirect diagnosis toward review execution when the failure was infrastructure-related, a timeout, or a cancellation.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:30-33,1012 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The existing root guard causes the parity test to fail and makes `_load_guard()` load the out-of-sync copy, causing four functional tests that depend on redirect stripping to fail.
  WHY: These failures make the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` check and aggregate lint check fail.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:36-39,1047 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Falling back to `TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH` when the root hook is absent makes the template parity test compare the template file with itself.
  WHY: The test passes tautologically instead of asserting root/template parity or explicitly requiring the root file.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A review/autofix failure is recorded by a marker, and the review job itself concludes success. The intake only read jobs that concluded failure." (PR DESCRIPTION, "The intake read no log at all for 8 review/autofix reports (`runs=0`)") — the focus-job fallback is intended to cover all review jobs that conclude success, not only the bare `codex-agent`/`…/codex-agent` patterns.
  expected_change_site: `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py` around the FOCUS_JOB_RE definition (line 88), and the parallel jq filter in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` at line ~270 (`test("(^|/\\s*)codex-agent$")`).
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: No diff hunk in either file changes the focus-job regex; both still require the literal `codex-agent$` end of name. The fix that closes the runs=0 gap for parenthesized-suffix job names is absent from the PR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py: line 88 (FOCUS_JOB_RE) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The regex `(?:^|/\s*)codex-agent$` does not match job names with a parenthesized suffix, so `select_jobs()` finds no focus job and skips the run.
  WHY: A review failure with a suffixed job name gets no sliced log in its evidence folder, recurring the runs=0 symptom.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: line 270 (jq filter in the "collect run summaries" loop, PR diff) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The jq `test("(^|/\\s*)codex-agent$")` filter does not match job names with a parenthesized suffix.
  WHY: The intake can read zero log files and provide no linked run to the diagnosis prompt.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py: lines 696-709 (Collector.lineage, PR diff) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `Collector.lineage` does not deduplicate paginated heal-labelled issues before building GraphQL aliases.
  WHY: A duplicate alias can make GitHub reject the query and skip all closing-PR lookups for related issues in the collection.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: line 689 (diagnosis prompt output, PR diff) | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `${failing_step:-none (review job)}` labels an empty failing step as a review job even for non-review jobs.
  WHY: A timed-out implement or clarify job can be diagnosed as a review failure, misdirecting root-cause analysis.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 30-33 and line 1012 (test_template_copies_are_identical) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: GUARD_PATH (.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py) exists in the repository but has diverged from TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH (workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py). Because GUARD_PATH exists on disk, lines 30-33 do not reassign it to TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH, causing test_template_copies_are_identical at line 1012 to fail. Additionally, _load_guard() loads the out-of-sync .claude copy rather than the updated template, causing 4 functional tests that depend on redirect stripping to fail.
  WHY: In the CI job tests-hooks-and-orchestrator, running pytest tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py fails with 5 failures, causing the tests-hooks-and-orchestrator check and the aggregate lint check to fail.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py: line 89: FOCUS_JOB_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|/\s*)codex-agent$") | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The regex does not match review jobs with a parenthesized suffix.
  WHY: `select_jobs()` returns an empty list and no job logs are collected, recurring the runs=0 symptom.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: line 270: jq selector for focus review jobs | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The jq selector anchors at the end of `codex-agent`, so it does not match `codex-agent (claude-branch-review)`.
  WHY: The intake finds no matching jobs and passes no job logs to the diagnosis prompt.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py: lines 825-850 in Collector.lineage() | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `Collector.lineage()` does not deduplicate issues by issue number before appending them to `related`.
  WHY: Duplicate GraphQL alias keys cause the query to fail and all PR closing references to be lost for the lineage.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: line 693: echo run header | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The log header defaults an empty `failing_step` to `none (review job)` for non-review workflow failures too.
  WHY: The prompt header can mislead the diagnosis model into treating an infrastructure failure as a successful review/autofix run.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py: lines 36-39 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Reassigning global GUARD_PATH = TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH when the root hook is absent makes the template parity test compare the template file with itself.
  WHY: The test passes tautologically rather than checking parity between distinct files or explicitly asserting that the root file exists.
